history.summary: The real referent of CSV 'Trikuta Parvata Temple' is the Trikutachal Mahadeva Temple in the dense forest atop Trikut Hill (Trikut Pahar), a three-peaked hill ~15 km from Deoghar in Mohanpur block on the Deoghar-Dumka road (CSV town 'Deoghar' is approximate; corrected detail here). The peaks (2,470 ft) are named for the Trimurti - Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva. The hilltop complex includes the Trikutachal Mahadeva Temple, the altar of Goddess Trishuli, Sage Dayananda's hermitage, the Belpatra Bagan (bel leaves collected here in Shravan for Baidyanath - hence 'Garden of Shiva'), Narayan Shila, Ravana's Helipad (legend: Ravana landed his Pushpak Vimana here), Sita Deep and Ravan Gupha. The Mayurakshi river originates here. A ropeway to the summit opened in 2003 (one source says 21 July 2009 - conflict) and was Jharkhand's first ropeway; it is non-operational since the April 2022 cable-car accident. Coordinates are the Wikipedia range coordinates for Trikut Hill.

name: Trikutachal Mahadeva Temple
town_description: Deoghar ('abode of gods') is a major Hindu pilgrimage city in the Santhal Pargana division of Jharkhand, famous for the Baidyanath Jyotirlinga temple. Trikut Hill lies ~15 km away in Mohanpur block, en route to Dumka.

travel.road: ~15 km from Deoghar on the Deoghar-Dumka road; summit reached by stairs/trekking (ropeway non-operational since April 2022 - verify current status)

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; avoid monsoon (clouds, slippery, waterfalls may be dangerous)
visitor_information.opening_hours: Hill open roughly 6 AM-6 PM; shrines accessible in daylight hours (verify locally)
